mvp-development.q: How much does an MVP cost?
mvp-development.a: A Validation MVP starts from £2,500, a Lean MVP from £5,000 and a Custom or SaaS platform from £10,000. Your price is agreed before any work starts. Not ready for an MVP yet? BUILD.ONE builds and tests your core feature in a week for £499. Our cost calculator gives you an instant estimate.
A Validation MVP takes 1–2 weeks and a Lean MVP 2–4 weeks. A Custom or SaaS platform usually takes around 8 weeks.

mvp-development.q: What if the idea doesn't validate?
mvp-development.a: Then you've saved months and most of your budget, and we'll help you work out what to test next.

mvp-development.q: Do I need a technical co-founder?
mvp-development.a: No. We act as your product and engineering team from validation to launch, and can help you hire in-house when the time is right.
You do. The code, designs and accounts are yours.
We review the data with you, fix what users struggle with and plan the next release. You can carry on with us as an ongoing partner.

prototype-to-production.a: The code audit is £750, fixed. The hardening sprint starts from £3,500, and we fix its price at the end of the audit. Book the sprint and the audit fee comes off it.

prototype-to-production.q: Which tools do you work with?
prototype-to-production.a: Apps built with Lovable, Bolt, Replit, Cursor, v0, Windsurf and similar, as well as code written with help from ChatGPT or Claude.
Only if it's the sensible option. We keep what's sound and fix what isn't, and the audit tells you which before you spend anything more.
The audit takes about a week. Most hardening sprints take 2–4 weeks, depending on what the audit finds.

prototype-to-production.q: What do you need from me?
prototype-to-production.a: Access to the code and the accounts it runs on, such as GitHub, Supabase and your hosting, plus a quick walk-through of what the app should do.

prototype-to-production.q: Can I keep building with AI tools afterwards?
prototype-to-production.a: Yes. We leave the code organised and tested, so you can carry on with AI tools or with us without breaking what's live.
You do. The code, accounts and documentation stay yours.

low-code-no-code.a: Launch starts from £2,500, Business from £5,000 and Advanced from £8,500. Your price is agreed before any work starts. Platform subscriptions are separate and sit in your name.

low-code-no-code.q: Is low-code good enough for real users?
low-code-no-code.a: For many products and internal tools, yes. We'll tell you honestly when custom code is the better choice.

low-code-no-code.q: Can we move to custom code later?
low-code-no-code.a: Yes. We design with that path in mind, so the switch is straightforward.
Yes. We train your team and document how everything works.
Bubble, Webflow, Softr, Shopify, Airtable, Supabase, Zapier, Make and n8n, chosen to fit what you need.
Subscriptions sit in your name, so you own the account. We'll recommend the right plan.
We use established platforms and set up user roles and permissions, so people only see what they should.

performance-marketing.a: Launch is £750 a month, Growth £1,250 a month and Scale from £2,000 a month. Your ad budget is separate from our fee.
It depends on your goals and market. We'll recommend a starting budget and scale what works.

performance-marketing.q: How soon will I see results?
performance-marketing.a: Early signals usually show within the first few weeks, then we optimise from there.

performance-marketing.q: Do you work with pre-launch products?
performance-marketing.a: Yes. Waitlist campaigns are one of the best ways to validate demand.
The ones your customers use. We research your audience first, then test the most promising channels with small budgets.
Yes. We write the copy and design the creative, then test variations to find what works.
Clear reports showing spend, results and cost per acquisition, with recommendations for what to do next.

web-mobile-apps.q: How much does an app cost?
web-mobile-apps.a: Web apps start from £5,000 (Starter), £8,500 (Business) and £15,000 (Advanced). Mobile apps for iOS and Android start from £7,500, £12,500 and £20,000. Your price is agreed before any work starts.

web-mobile-apps.q: Do you build native or cross-platform apps?
web-mobile-apps.a: Usually cross-platform with React Native or Flutter, so one codebase serves iOS and Android. We'll recommend native when it's genuinely needed.

web-mobile-apps.q: Can you take over an existing app?
web-mobile-apps.a: Yes. We start with a code review, then fix, improve or rebuild depending on what's there.

web-mobile-apps.q: Will you publish to the App Store and Google Play?
web-mobile-apps.a: Yes, we handle submission and review for both stores.
The one that fits your product, team and budget. We explain the options in plain English and recommend what will last, not what's trendy.

web-mobile-apps.q: How do you keep apps secure?
web-mobile-apps.a: Encrypted connections, secure authentication, role-based access and regular dependency updates, with GDPR in mind from the start.

web-mobile-apps.q: Do you support apps after launch?
web-mobile-apps.a: Yes. We offer ongoing maintenance, monitoring and new feature development.

ecommerce-marketplace-development.q: How much does an online store or marketplace cost?
ecommerce-marketplace-development.a: An online store starts at £1,000 (Basic, on Shopify, WooCommerce or custom-built), with Growth from £2,000 and Advanced from £3,500. A marketplace starts from £5,000 (Launch), with Growth from £8,500 and Scale from £15,000. Your price is agreed before any work starts.
Yes. TechClues is a Shopify Partner. We design, build and set up Shopify stores, and build on WooCommerce or custom code where that fits you better.

ecommerce-marketplace-development.q: Should I use Shopify, WooCommerce or a custom build?
ecommerce-marketplace-development.a: Shopify suits most shops that want to start selling quickly. WooCommerce suits businesses already on WordPress. A custom build makes sense for marketplaces and buying flows the platforms can't handle. We'll recommend one before we start.

ecommerce-marketplace-development.q: Can you build a multi-vendor marketplace?
ecommerce-marketplace-development.a: Yes. Sellers can sign up, list their products and get paid, while you set the rules, approve listings and take a commission.

ecommerce-marketplace-development.q: Can you move my existing shop?
ecommerce-marketplace-development.a: Usually, yes. We'll check what can move from your current platform, such as products, customers and orders, when we scope the work.
Cards and digital wallets through providers such as Stripe, PayPal or Shopify Payments, set up for UK VAT.
You do. The store, its content and your customer data are yours, and platform accounts are set up in your name.

ecommerce-marketplace-development.q: Can you help us get sales after launch?
ecommerce-marketplace-development.a: Yes. Our performance marketing team runs paid social and Google Ads campaigns to bring in customers.

ui-ux-design.a: Essential starts from £1,000, Product from £2,000 and Complete from £3,500. Your price is agreed before any work starts, and you own the design files.

ui-ux-design.q: Do you only design, or build too?
ui-ux-design.a: Both. You can hire us for design only, or design and build together for a smoother handover.

ui-ux-design.q: Will I own the design files?
ui-ux-design.a: Yes. You get the full Figma files and design system.
With clickable prototypes and short sessions with real or target users.
It depends on scope. Design for a focused MVP fits inside the 2–4 week MVP timeline; larger products take longer.
Yes. We design to WCAG guidelines, covering contrast, type size, focus states and screen reader support.

ui-ux-design.q: Can you work with our existing brand?
ui-ux-design.a: Yes. We'll extend your brand into a product design system, or refine it where it needs help.

industries-healthcare-medical.q: Do you build to NHS and GDPR standards?
industries-healthcare-medical.a: We design with GDPR and relevant NHS Digital standards in mind from day one, and plan compliance needs during discovery.

industries-healthcare-medical.q: Can you integrate with our existing systems?
industries-healthcare-medical.a: Yes. We connect patient management, EHR/EMR and booking systems through their APIs or standard formats.

industries-healthcare-medical.q: Can you build a medical device app?
industries-healthcare-medical.a: We can build the software and plan for MHRA guidance where it applies. Regulatory sign-off stays with you and your advisers.
Yes. Many healthcare products start with a focused MVP, such as online booking, and grow from there.

industries-retail-ecommerce.q: Do you build on Shopify or custom?
industries-retail-ecommerce.a: Both routes are possible. We recommend a platform when it fits, and custom builds when you need something it can't do.
Yes, including seller onboarding, split payments, commissions and reviews.

industries-retail-ecommerce.q: Can you connect to our stock system?
industries-retail-ecommerce.a: Yes. We integrate with inventory, ERP and point-of-sale systems through their APIs.

industries-retail-ecommerce.q: Can you help us grow after launch?
industries-retail-ecommerce.a: Yes. Our performance marketing team runs campaigns and tests to improve conversion.

industries-pre-seed-seed-startups.q: How much does a startup MVP cost?
industries-pre-seed-seed-startups.a: A Validation MVP starts from £2,500, a Lean MVP from £5,000 and a Custom or SaaS platform from £10,000, with your price agreed before any work starts. Try our cost calculator for an instant estimate.
A Lean MVP usually takes 2–4 weeks, and a Validation MVP to test demand first takes 1–2 weeks.

industries-pre-seed-seed-startups.q: Can you help with our pitch?
industries-pre-seed-seed-startups.a: We can build prototypes and product demos that make your pitch concrete.
That's what validation is for. We keep builds lean so changing direction is affordable.

industries-saas-startups.q: Can you build our SaaS from scratch?
industries-saas-startups.a: Yes, from validation and design to billing, dashboards and launch.
Yes. We set up plans, trials, upgrades and invoicing, usually with Stripe.

industries-saas-startups.q: Can you take over our existing product?
industries-saas-startups.a: Yes. We start with a code review, then improve or rebuild what's needed.

industries-saas-startups.q: How do you keep customer data separate?
industries-saas-startups.a: With a multi-tenant architecture and role-based access built in from the start.

industries-logistics-transportation.q: Can you connect to our existing TMS or WMS?
industries-logistics-transportation.a: Yes. We integrate through APIs or data feeds, or replace legacy tools step by step.

industries-logistics-transportation.q: Do driver apps work without signal?
industries-logistics-transportation.a: Yes. We build offline-first apps that sync when a connection returns.

industries-logistics-transportation.q: Can you add live tracking for customers?
industries-logistics-transportation.a: Yes, with tracking links, delivery windows and notifications by SMS or email.
Usually with the biggest bottleneck, such as dispatch or tracking, as a focused first release.

industries-education-consulting.q: Should we use an off-the-shelf LMS?
industries-education-consulting.a: Sometimes that's the right call. We build custom when you need your own brand, flows or business model.

industries-education-consulting.q: Can we sell courses and sessions online?
industries-education-consulting.a: Yes, with one-off payments, subscriptions and bundles.

industries-education-consulting.q: Can you build a client portal for our consultancy?
industries-education-consulting.a: Yes, with secure document sharing, updates and messaging.
Yes. A low-code first version can go live fast, then grow into custom code.

industries-recruitment-staffing.q: Can you integrate with our ATS or CRM?
industries-recruitment-staffing.a: Yes. We connect through their APIs, or automate between tools where APIs are limited.

industries-recruitment-staffing.q: Can you build a job board?
industries-recruitment-staffing.a: Yes, with search, alerts, applications and multi-posting to other boards.

industries-recruitment-staffing.q: Do you use AI for matching?
industries-recruitment-staffing.a: Where it helps. AI can rank and summarise candidates, with consultants making the final call.

industries-recruitment-staffing.q: How do you handle candidate data?
industries-recruitment-staffing.a: With GDPR in mind: clear consent, retention rules and easy data requests.

industries-industry-manufacturing.q: Can you connect to our ERP or machines?
industries-industry-manufacturing.a: Yes. We integrate with ERP and MES systems and can collect machine data through sensors or gateways.

industries-industry-manufacturing.q: Will the apps work on the shop floor?
industries-industry-manufacturing.a: Yes. We design for tablets, gloves and noisy environments, with offline support where needed.
Yes. We usually digitise one process first, such as maintenance, then expand.
Where it makes sense. Often we connect to them first and replace them gradually.

brand-strategy.a: Essential starts from £750, Identity from £1,500 and Complete from £2,500. Your price is agreed before any work starts, and you get editable files.
We can, but the best results come from positioning first, then the identity that expresses it.
Logo files, colour and type system, brand guidelines and any launch assets we agree.

brand-strategy.q: Can you refresh an existing brand?
brand-strategy.a: Yes. We'll keep what works and evolve the rest.

brand-strategy.q: How long does a brand project take?
brand-strategy.a: It depends on scope. A focused identity is quicker than a full strategy; we'll give you a clear timeline before we start.
Yes: vector logo files, colour codes, font details and editable templates.

brand-strategy.q: Can you apply the brand to our website?
brand-strategy.a: Yes. We can carry your new brand straight into your website or product.

partners.a: Anyone who meets businesses that need software, apps, AI, design or marketing: agencies without a development team, freelancers, business advisers, accountants, startup communities and past clients. We approve each partner. TechClues staff can't take part.

10% of our fees up to £20,000, and 5% of anything above that, up to £5,000 a referral. For monthly services, the same on the first 6 months' fees. A BUILD.ONE earns a flat £50. Pro partners, with 3 or more paid referrals in 12 months, earn 12.5% on the first £20,000. Further work from the same client within 12 months of their first payment earns 5%.

partners.q: How do I register a referral?
partners.a: Use the "Refer a client" form on this page, or email info@techclues.co.uk with you and the client both copied, before their first call with us. Only refer people who have agreed to us contacting them. We confirm in writing whether the referral is registered, and the commission it qualifies for.

When the client is new to us (not in touch with us in the previous 6 months), signs within 6 months of your referral, and pays. If two partners introduce the same client, the first registered referral counts.
What the client pays us, excluding VAT and third-party costs such as ad spend, hosting, software licences and app store fees. An audit fee that's credited against a build is counted once.

partners.q: When and how am I paid?
partners.a: By bank transfer in pounds, within 14 days of each client payment clearing. When a project is paid in stages, commission is paid in stages too. Businesses send us an invoice, and you're responsible for your own tax.

partners.q: What if a client cancels or gets a refund?
partners.a: Commission is due only on what the client pays and keeps paying. If we refund a payment, the commission on it comes off your next payout.

partners.q: What should I tell the people I refer?
partners.a: That you may earn a referral fee. Please don't promise prices, timelines or results on our behalf: we'll quote after a call.
We may change the rates for future referrals, with notice. A referral we've registered keeps the commission we confirmed. The full terms come with your welcome email.

faq-getting-started.a: We design and build digital products: MVPs, custom platforms, web and mobile apps, and the brand and interface around them. Most of our work is taking an idea to something real people can use.

faq-getting-started.q: How do I start a project with you?
faq-getting-started.a: Book the free 30-minute strategy call. We'll talk through your idea, what you're trying to prove and what it would take to build, and you'll leave with a plan whether or not you work with us.

faq-getting-started.q: What happens on the first call?
faq-getting-started.a: Questions, mostly ours. We want the problem, the people you're building for and the outcome you need. If we're a fit, we follow up with scope, cost and a timeline.

faq-getting-started.q: Do I need a finished spec before we talk?
faq-getting-started.a: No. A paragraph and a rough idea of who it's for is enough. Turning that into a scope is part of what we do.

faq-getting-started.q: Do you work with non-technical founders?
faq-getting-started.a: Most of our clients are non-technical. We explain trade-offs in plain terms and never ask you to pick a database.

faq-getting-started.q: Can you take over a product someone else started?
faq-getting-started.a: Often, yes. We'll review what exists first and tell you honestly whether it's better to continue it or rebuild the parts that are holding you back.

faq-getting-started.q: Do you work with clients outside the UK?
faq-getting-started.a: Yes. We're based in West Midlands and work with founders elsewhere over calls and shared documents; the process doesn't change.

faq-getting-started.q: How do I know whether to build an MVP or the full product?
faq-getting-started.a: If any important assumption is still a guess, build the MVP. If the demand is proven and you're solving a known problem, going straight to the full build can be the cheaper route.

faq-pricing.q: How much does an MVP cost?
faq-pricing.a: It depends on the features, the platforms and the pace. The MVP cost calculator gives you a range in a couple of minutes, and the call turns that into a firm number.

faq-pricing.q: How accurate is the cost calculator?
faq-pricing.a: It's a planning range, not a quote. It's built from what we've charged for similar work, but the final figure comes after we've scoped your project properly.

faq-pricing.q: Why do estimates vary so much between agencies?
faq-pricing.a: Mostly scope and seniority. A cheap quote usually means fewer features, less testing or a junior team; ask anyone quoting you what's excluded.
Design, development, testing and launch of the scope we agree. Third-party costs like hosting, payment processing or paid AI usage sit outside it.

faq-pricing.q: Do you charge per project or by the hour?
faq-pricing.a: We price the agreed scope, so you know the figure before we start rather than watching a meter run.
Payment terms are set out in the proposal and tied to milestones, so nothing is due before you've seen progress against it.

faq-pricing.q: What happens if the scope changes mid-project?
faq-pricing.a: We tell you what it costs in time and money before anything is built, and you decide. Small changes usually absorb; new features are quoted.

faq-pricing.q: Are there ongoing costs after launch?
faq-pricing.a: Hosting, domains and any paid services your product uses are billed by those providers. Ongoing development or support is optional and agreed separately.
Milestone payments already spread the cost across the project. If you need something different, raise it on the call and we'll tell you straight whether it works.

faq-process.a: A validation MVP takes 2–4 weeks. Larger platforms are usually around 8 weeks, depending on scope.

faq-process.q: What are the stages of a project?
faq-process.a: Eight: Ignition, Compass, Pillar, Canvas, Forge, Bridge, Sentinel and Everest — idea and research, then planning, design, build, integrations, QA and launch.

faq-process.q: What do you need from me during the build?
faq-process.a: Decisions, quickly, and access to anyone who knows your users. An hour a week of your time is typical; slow decisions are the usual cause of slow projects.

faq-process.q: How often will I hear from you?
faq-process.a: Weekly at minimum, with something to look at rather than a status update. You'll have a direct line to the people building it.

faq-process.q: Can you work to a fixed launch date?
faq-process.a: Yes, provided the scope can move. Fixed date and fixed scope at the same time is where projects go wrong.

faq-process.q: What if I need it faster?
faq-process.a: We can put more people on it, which costs more per week but shortens the calendar. The calculator's pace options show the effect.
We build in short cycles with something reviewable at the end of each one, so you're never waiting weeks to see where the project is.

faq-process.q: What usually slows a project down?
faq-process.a: Waiting on content, waiting on access to a third-party system, and mid-build changes of direction. We flag all three early.

faq-process.q: Can we start before everything is decided?
faq-process.a: Yes. We start with the parts we're sure of and design the rest so that later decisions don't force a rebuild.

faq-mvp.a: The smallest version of your product that tests the assumption your business depends on. Not a demo, not half a product — something real users can complete a real task with.

faq-mvp.q: How do you decide what goes into the first version?
faq-mvp.a: We work back from the assumption you need to test. Anything that doesn't help prove or disprove it waits for version two.

faq-mvp.q: What if the idea doesn't validate?
faq-mvp.a: Then you've saved the cost of building it. That's the point: we'd rather kill a bad idea in week two than bill you for six months of it.

faq-mvp.q: Do you do research before building?
faq-mvp.a: Yes. Understanding the users and the existing alternatives is part of the early stages, not an optional extra.

faq-mvp.q: Can you help us get the first users?
faq-mvp.a: We've run waitlist and launch campaigns alongside builds — Infinite Running League had over 1,000 sign-ups before any code was written.
Not the way we build it. It's a smaller product, not a worse one, and it's built so the next version extends it rather than replaces it.
A free stress test. You describe the idea, we aim at the customer, the alternatives, the differentiation, the scope and the risks, and tell you what to validate first.

faq-design.q: Do you design as well as build?
faq-design.a: Yes. UI/UX design and prototyping are part of the process, and we also do brand and identity work when a product needs one.

faq-design.q: Will I see designs before development starts?
faq-design.a: Always. You get a clickable prototype to walk through, so changes happen in design where they're cheap.

faq-design.q: Do you follow our brand or create one?
faq-design.a: Either. If you have brand guidelines we work inside them; if you don't, we can create the identity alongside the product.

faq-design.q: Can you test the design with real users?
faq-design.a: Yes, that's what the prototype is for. Watching a handful of people use it before we build is the cheapest research there is.
Figma, with Framer and Maze alongside it for prototyping and testing.
We build to sensible accessibility standards — contrast, keyboard use, screen-reader labelling — as a default, and we can go further if you're held to a specific standard.

faq-design.q: Do we get the design files?
faq-design.a: Yes. The design files are yours along with the rest of the work.

faq-technology.a: React and Next.js on the front end, Node, Python or .NET on the back end, PostgreSQL or MongoDB for data, hosted on AWS, Google Cloud, Azure or Vercel. Flutter and React Native for mobile.
We recommend, you decide. The choice follows what the product needs and what your team can maintain, not what's fashionable.
Yes, for iOS and Android. Whether you need one on day one is a different question, and often the answer is no.

faq-technology.q: Web app or mobile app first?
faq-technology.a: Web first, usually. It's faster to build, easier to change and there's no app store review between you and your users.

faq-technology.q: When do you use low-code or no-code?
faq-technology.a: When speed matters more than a custom build — internal tools, simple marketplaces, storefronts. We use Shopify, Webflow, Bubble, Softr and automation tools like Zapier, Make and n8n, and we'll tell you when custom code is the better call.

faq-technology.q: Can you integrate with the systems we already use?
faq-technology.a: Yes. Payments, CRMs, email, maps, analytics and internal APIs are routine; integrations are a stage of our process, not an afterthought.
Roles and permissions, sensible authentication, encrypted connections, and access limited to what each user needs. If you're handling sensitive data, tell us early so it shapes the architecture.
Quality assurance is its own stage: we test across devices and browsers, and fix what we find before launch rather than after.
We build the foundation to scale from the start, so the first version doesn't have to be thrown away when traffic arrives.

faq-ai.q: What can you actually build with AI?
faq-ai.a: Assistants that answer from your own content, generated copy and images, document and data extraction, search that understands intent, and automations that remove manual steps.

faq-ai.q: Can you add AI to our existing product?
faq-ai.a: Yes. That's most of this work: integrating models into a product that already exists rather than starting again.
Whichever fits the job — Claude, OpenAI and Gemini models, with LangChain and Hugging Face tooling around them. We'll weigh accuracy, speed and cost per use before recommending one.

faq-ai.q: Is our data used to train someone else's model?
faq-ai.a: Not with the enterprise and API arrangements we build on, where training on your data is off by default. We confirm the terms of whichever provider you choose before we wire it in.

faq-ai.q: How do you keep AI answers accurate?
faq-ai.a: Ground them in your own content, constrain what the model is allowed to answer, and show sources where it matters. We also test the awkward questions, not just the easy ones.

faq-ai.q: What does an AI feature add to the cost?
faq-ai.a: The build cost is in the calculator; the running cost depends on usage and the model you pick. We'll size both before you commit.

faq-ai.q: Should my MVP have AI in it?
faq-ai.a: Only if it's doing real work for the user. AI that's there to be mentioned in the pitch deck adds cost and risk without adding value.

faq-launch.a: We deploy, monitor it, and stay close for the first stretch of real usage — that's the Everest stage of our process.
We set it up and can manage it for you. The hosting itself is billed by the provider, so you keep ownership of the account.

faq-launch.q: What if we find a bug after launch?
faq-launch.a: Tell us. If it's something we built and it isn't doing what we agreed, we fix it.
Yes, as an ongoing arrangement agreed separately. Plenty of clients keep us for a few days a month; others take it in-house.

faq-launch.q: Can our own developers take it over?
faq-launch.a: Yes. We hand over the code, the accounts and the documentation, and we'll walk your team through it.

faq-launch.q: Do we get the source code?
faq-launch.a: Yes. The product and the code we write for it are yours.

faq-launch.q: Can you keep building after launch?
faq-launch.a: That's usually the plan. The first version teaches you what to build next, and we'll keep going for as long as it's useful.

faq-working-together.a: West Midlands, at 125 Hazelville Road. We work with clients across the UK and beyond, and we're happy to meet in person if you're nearby.

faq-working-together.q: Who will I work with day to day?
faq-working-together.a: The people building your product. There's no account manager relaying messages between you and the team.
Yes, and we already work under NDAs for several clients. Ask before you share anything sensitive and we'll get it signed.
You do. The product, the designs and the code are yours.

faq-working-together.q: Will our project appear in your portfolio?
faq-working-together.a: Only with your permission. Where we're under an NDA, details stay confidential — which is why some of our case studies are deliberately light on specifics.

faq-working-together.q: Do you work under a contract?
faq-working-together.a: Always. Scope, timeline, cost and terms are agreed in writing before work starts.

faq-working-together.q: What if we're not happy with something?
faq-working-together.a: Say so early. Short cycles exist precisely so you can redirect us in week one rather than week six.
Email info@techclues.co.uk, call +44 7472 411699, or book the free strategy call. During a project you'll have a shared channel with the team.

faq-fit.q: Which industries do you work in?
faq-fit.a: Healthcare, logistics and transport, retail and e-commerce, education and consulting, funded startups, recruitment and staffing, SaaS, and industry and manufacturing.

faq-fit.q: Do you work in regulated industries?
faq-fit.a: We've built for healthcare and finance-adjacent products. Tell us the rules you're held to early and they shape the design rather than arriving as a surprise at the end.

faq-fit.q: Do you only work with startups?
faq-fit.a: No. Plenty of our work is for established businesses replacing spreadsheets and disconnected tools with one product.

faq-fit.q: We're pre-funding. Can you still help?
faq-fit.a: Yes, and the MVP route exists for exactly that position — something real to show users and investors without spending the round you haven't raised yet.

faq-fit.q: Can you help with a funding round?
faq-fit.a: We can't raise it for you, but a working product and evidence that people use it is the most persuasive thing you can take into the room.

faq-fit.q: Do you take equity instead of fees?
faq-fit.a: Our default is a straightforward fee. If you want to discuss something else, raise it on the call and we'll give you a direct answer.

faq-fit.q: Is there work you turn down?
faq-fit.a: Yes — when we don't think we're the right people for it, or when the plan is to build something nobody has checked anyone wants. We'll say so rather than take the project.

grant-funding.a: No. Funding decisions are made by the grant provider, and most schemes are competitive. We help you find schemes that fit and put forward the strongest application we can.
Checking your options is free, with no obligation. If you'd like us to prepare an application, we agree the scope and cost with you before any work starts.
It changes through the year and depends on where you're based, your sector and the project. Our UK funding guide lists what's open now, what's paused and what's coming.
Most schemes are for small and medium-sized businesses, and many only cover one nation or region of the UK. That's why the form asks where you're based and how big the business is.

grant-funding.q: Can you build the project as well?
grant-funding.a: Yes. We design and build websites, software, automation and AI, so the plan in your application and the build that follows line up.

zero-one.q: Can I show it to investors?
zero-one.a: Yes, that's what it's built for. A working feature on a live link, plus feedback from real users, gives you something real to show potential investors, co-founders and early customers.

zero-one.q: Will it help with a grant application?
zero-one.a: It can. Innovation funders usually want evidence that people need what you're building, and a tested prototype with findings from real users gives you something concrete to point to. It doesn't guarantee funding: the funder decides. If you'd like help with the application itself, we offer grant application support too.
No. It's a smaller product: one feature, one week and one question answered, so you know whether to invest in a full MVP.

zero-one.q: What counts as the core feature?
zero-one.a: The one thing your product must do for someone to care. If it needs logins, payments or an admin panel to work, it's bigger than BUILD.ONE, and we'll suggest a Validation or Lean MVP instead.
Five people you invite: potential customers from your network or audience. We run the sessions and write up what we learn.

zero-one.q: What if I can't find five testers?
zero-one.a: Tell us on the kick-off call. It's a useful signal in itself, and we'll talk through the best way to reach your first users before the build starts.
You get a findings note and a debrief with a clear recommendation. If you go ahead with any build within 30 days, the £499 comes off it.
Each BUILD.ONE gets a full week of focus, so we take on one a week.

calculator.a: It gives an estimated range based on the features, platform and pace you choose. It's a realistic starting point; the final cost depends on detailed requirements, integrations and custom work.

calculator.q: What affects the cost of an MVP?
calculator.a: The number of core features, web or mobile, design complexity, third-party integrations such as payments or APIs, and your timeline. As these grow, so does the effort and the cost.

calculator.q: What is included in an MVP?
calculator.a: Only the essentials needed to test your core idea: usually user accounts, the main functionality, a simple dashboard and any must-have integrations.

calculator.q: Can you help refine my idea?
calculator.a: Yes. We work with founders to validate ideas, choose the right features and design an MVP that launches quickly within budget.

calculator.q: What should I do after getting my estimate?
calculator.a: Refine your scope and plan your roadmap. Book a free call and we'll turn your estimate into a detailed plan and proposal.

calculator.q: Can the MVP grow into a full product?
calculator.a: Yes. We build MVPs to scale, so once the idea is validated you can add features and integrations rather than start again.

home.a: We're an MVP studio in West Midlands. We help founders validate ideas, then design, build and scale them.

home.q: How much does an MVP cost?
home.a: A Validation MVP starts from £2,500, a Lean MVP from £5,000 and a Custom or SaaS platform from £10,000, with your price agreed before any work starts. Try our cost calculator for an instant estimate.

home.q: How long does it take to build an MVP?
home.a: A Validation MVP takes 1–2 weeks and a Lean MVP 2–4 weeks. A Custom or SaaS platform takes around 8 weeks, agreed up front.

home.q: How does TechClues develop an MVP?
home.a: Through eight phases: Ignition, Compass, Pillar, Canvas, Forge, Bridge, Sentinel and Everest, from first idea to deployment.

home.q: Can you turn an MVP into a full product?
home.a: Yes. We build on scalable foundations from day one, so nothing gets thrown away.

home.q: How do you support products after launch?
home.a: Ongoing support, maintenance and growth marketing once you're live.

ai-enablement.a: Most projects start with an AI audit: £1,500, over about two weeks. Builds start from £3,000 and are priced at the end of the audit. If you go ahead, the audit fee comes off the build.

ai-enablement.q: Can you add AI to our existing product?
ai-enablement.a: Yes. That's the most common request: we connect a model to your data and build the feature into the product you already run.

ai-enablement.q: Will our data be used to train models?
ai-enablement.a: We configure providers so your content isn't used for training, and we agree up front what data may leave your systems.

ai-enablement.q: How do you stop it making things up?
ai-enablement.a: We ground answers in your documents, show sources, test against real examples before launch and add fallbacks for when the model isn't confident.

ai-enablement.q: What does it cost to run?
ai-enablement.a: Most providers charge by usage, so cost follows how much you use it. We estimate it during the prototype and monitor spend after launch.

ai-enablement.q: Do we need a lot of data?
ai-enablement.a: Not for most work. Retrieval works with the documents you already have; fine-tuning needs more, and we'll say if it's worth it.
Whichever suits the task and budget, including Claude, OpenAI and Gemini. We keep the integration swappable so you're not locked in.

staff-augmentation.q: How is this different from a full project outsourcing engagement?
staff-augmentation.a: You keep full ownership of the roadmap and management; we add engineering capacity into your existing team rather than taking over delivery.
Typically within a few weeks from scoping to start date, depending on the specialisation required.

staff-augmentation.q: Can we interview candidates before they join?
staff-augmentation.a: Yes, we share matched candidates for your approval before onboarding. Team size or roles can also flex as your roadmap shifts.

staff-augmentation.q: Do you handle payroll and employment, or do we?
staff-augmentation.a: TechClues handles employment, payroll, and benefits; you manage day-to-day work.

staff-augmentation.q: Can this scale up or down as our project changes?
staff-augmentation.a: Yes, headcount flexes with your roadmap without a hiring or layoff cycle on your end.

staff-augmentation.q: Who owns the code, models, and IP built by embedded engineers?
staff-augmentation.a: You do. All code, AI models, and data pipelines built during the engagement belong to your organisation.

staff-augmentation.q: What is the difference between nearshore, onshore, and offshore?
staff-augmentation.a: Nearshore gives close time zone overlap at lower cost than onshore; onshore puts engineers in your own region; offshore operates from our global delivery centres as a cost-efficient extension of your team.

game-development.q: What game engines do you develop with?
game-development.a: Unity and Unreal Engine, with native pipelines for VR and XR and UEFN using Verse. Art is produced in Blender and 3DS Max, shipped cross-platform across mobile, PC and console.

game-development.q: What are the two ways to work with your studio?
game-development.a: As a dedicated extension of your team when you need delivery power, or as the studio behind your player-facing title when you need an idea built end to end.

game-development.q: Do you build metaverse titles with real ownership mechanics?
game-development.a: Yes. We build metaverse and MMO titles with wallet sign-in, digital collectibles and ownable land wired into real gameplay loops.

game-development.q: What is UEFN development, and do you build for it?
game-development.a: UEFN, the Unreal Editor for Fortnite, lets studios publish custom games inside Fortnite using Verse. We build bespoke islands using this pipeline.

game-development.q: Do you do architectural visualisation outside of games?
game-development.a: Yes. We deliver real-time property tours and architectural walkthroughs built on the same engines.

game-development.q: How much does game development cost?
game-development.a: Cost depends on scope, platform and art fidelity. A prototype or vertical slice is a fixed, lower-cost starting point.
